newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares close higher with small gains.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares close higher with small gains.

text.p: ** (1230 GMT) - Shares at major Indian exchanges end with
small gains as markets stage technical recovery
** Bombay's benchmark share index closes 36.50 pts, or 0.98
pct, up at 3,762.37, off 3,796.78--intra-day high
** Markets seem to settle down, but foreign funds stay
quiet, no major buying action seen--traders
** National Stock Exchange 50-stock index ends 22.2 pts,
or 2.11 percent, higher at 1074.2 in extended trade
** Delhi share index falls 9.65 pts, to 776.71, but Madras
inches up 8.04 pts to 3,539.34
Shares at Indian bourses failed to build up on an early technical recovery on Wednesday due to lack of foreign fund buying, but ended higher, dealers said.
"The market was better than yesterday, but we saw lacklustre trade," said Yogendra Shah, director at YSN Shares Pvt Ltd.
The morning rebound reversed four straight days of declines when the benchmark Bombay share index lost 218.74 points, or over five percent.
"I guess, hesitation on the part of foreign funds and lack of support from domestic institutions weighed on the market," Shah said.

Bolstered by a budget widely hailed as market-friendly, Bombay shares raced ahead last week, with the top 30-share index surging to an eight month-high of 4,029.56. It rose nearly 16 percent after the February 28, 1997/98 (April-March), budget.

"This is a steady market. People were expecting foreign funds to rush in, but they are cautious buyers," said a dealer at a foreign securities firm. "Funds are not jumping in. There would be slow and steady business coming in," the dealer added.
Under the budget proposals, the government slashed corporate and personal income tax rates, hiked foreign portfolio limit in firms and allowed companies to buy back their own shares.
Shares at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) closed higher than Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) due to renewed buying on the first day of the weekly account.
"The difference in closing rates among both exchanges should lead to a firm Thursday opening," said a local dealer. Activity was concentrated in heavily traded stocks, he said.
Selective buying by local mutual funds failed to offset sales by foreign investors and speculators which pushed Delhi shares to a lower close, dealers said.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
